summary: Grow / Shrink mask slider in MpiMaskStrip, so every mask tool gets it at once. Leading mechanism: blur plus an SVG feFuncA alpha threshold on Canvas2D = real-time dilate/erode at the 1536 working size; sharp is the fallback because it is a round trip per drag. Traps: compounding (derive every frame from a drag-start snapshot) and which layer to grow (maskCanvas is derived; a bake into manual must respect the MPI-371 layer order). Sequenced after MPI-380.

maturity idea -> planned. approach and fallback are both settled (canvas blur plus an alpha threshold, Sharp server-side as the fallback), and the card now carries the whole strip control pack. Board-wide re-stamp against the grown 10-value enum (todo gained research / needs-decision / blocked / deferred on 2026-07-31); every todo card had been sitting on idea or planned because those were the only values that existed when it was written.

Picked up by the user as step 1 of the MPI-424 umbrella, replacing the rejected MPI-379. Asked what to start with, he named both halves of this card unprompted: the slider that expands and shrinks the current mask, and turning a mask into just its edges with TWO sliders, one expanding outward and one inward - which is the MPI-400 half absorbed into this card earlier the same day. They are one primitive, not two: an edge band is dilate(outward) minus erode(inward), so the blur-plus-alpha-threshold mechanism gets written once and read three ways. Moved to doing for the DESIGN session; no implementation before the design is agreed. Open questions the card already carries: which layer grows (maskCanvas is derived by _recomposite so writing to it is pointless), whether the drag holds live at the 1536 working size, and the compounding trap - every frame must derive from the pristine drag-start snapshot, which UndoStack.pendingLayer already provides.

Back to todo: the DESIGN is complete but it cannot be built until MPI-425 declares the Adjust button. Re-scoped from a shared-strip control to its own tool in the Mask group - the strip could not host it, because Add/Subtract live in MpiMaskDetectRow and exist only on Detect and Points, so a strip slider would have had no commit control on the Brush tool, and Add/Subtract cannot express an edge band anyway since a ring REPLACES the mask. Agreed design: one Grow/Shrink slider, an Edge button that swaps that row for Outward + Inward, live pending-green preview, Apply + Reset, discard on leave. Bake-on-release was rejected by name - dilate-then-erode is a morphological close, so dragging back is not a restore. The alpha brush pack absorbed into this card earlier the same day moves to MPI-375, where the brush engine is extracted.

Planned. plan.md written. Grew a STEP 1 the card did not have: the PREVIEW CONTRACT. Verified in code that an unapplied Detect preview never dies - _exitAutoMaskMode(false) in MpiCanvasViewer.js:713 drops the picks, preserves manual+subtract and re-emits mask-ready/mask-clear, and it has NO CALLER; commitAutoMask (line 1352) has none either; mountOptions() destroys the outgoing options compound on every rail switch and never touches the picks. So a detection survives a tool switch and reaches the graph without Add - which is exactly MPI-365 open item. User settled it 2026-08-02 and generalised it to the whole family: every tool is visited, previewed, then applied, or the preview goes away, because surviving previews stack and the user ends up judging a composite he never committed to. Doing it first also dissolves the layer-order problem - with picks gone, Adjust only ever sees manual minus subtract, so the MPI-371 union-last rule cannot interact with a shrink. Accepted cost: Add becomes mandatory. Also healed acceptance 1 and 5, which still said in MpiMaskStrip and baked once on release - both overridden by the 2026-08-01 re-scope on the same card. Mechanism stays blur-plus-alpha-threshold first (needs calibrating against a known circle), with circular-offset stamping as the exact fallback; sharp server-side is ruled out, a round trip per drag frame is not live. Verify mode user-ux. Card stays todo/planned - implementation runs through mpi-continue.

Implementation started. Step 1 is the preview contract - wire the existing but uncalled _exitAutoMaskMode(false) to a single discard seam in mountOptions(), so no unapplied preview outlives its tool; step 2 is the Adjust tool itself. Checklist derived from plan.md, validation.md seeded. Verify mode user-ux.
Checklist derived from plan.md: the preview contract, then the Adjust tool.
Step 1 (the preview contract) checked off; step 2 (the Adjust tool) still open.

Step 1 of 2 SHIPPED and user-verified in the app: THE PREVIEW CONTRACT. el.discardPreview() on MpiCanvasViewer is the one seam, called by mountOptions() on every rail switch and guarded so a preview-less switch does nothing. Found while wiring it that _exitAutoMaskMode(false) was only three quarters written - it cleared the canvas auto layers and the persisted entry but NOT _autoMaskPicks, _lastDetectThumbUrls or the thumb strip, so calling it verbatim would have left the strip advertising picks for pixels that no longer existed; all four now drop together. tests/preview-contract.test.cjs adds 5 tests, three of them negative-controlled against the real source. Suite 310 pass / 0 fail, lint 0 errors on both configs. docs/masking.md was already 211 lines - OVER its own 200 cap before this session - and the remaining prose is load-bearing, so the tool-family half was SPLIT into docs/masking-tools.md (128 + 124) rather than trimmed, the third such split after masking-sam3 and masking-undo, with routing updated in docs/README.md and the CLAUDE.md context router. User verified live: no flicker, undo still correct, brush strokes survive the switch. Step 2 (the Adjust tool itself) NOT started - card stays in doing. Side effect: this closes MPI-365 open detected-but-not-applied mask is still injected item.
